newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude surges $1 in a technically-driven move.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude surges $1 in a technically-driven move.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures surged to close nearly $1.00 a barrel higher Monday as a number of weekend events pushed the front-month through a key level and triggered a wave of technical buying.
June crude oil futures closed up 95 cents at $21.38, having peaked at $21.55 a barrel, after gapping up at the open through a key technical resistance level just above $20.50.
However, some traders and analysts were skeptical that there was much behind the move.

"Like last week's advance...today's gains are a result of fear and 'short' vulnerability rather than any change in actual supply," said Tim Evans, an analyst at Pegasus Econometrics Group, a unit of Thomson Research.
"That's not to say it can't continue and it is possible June 'shorts' will remain on the defensive into next Tuesday's contract expiration," Evans said.

"We're not sure what is going on but there were a lot of options 'called' on Friday night (over about one million barrels) and then they seemed to be buying it up this morning," said a dealer at a major commodities trading firm.

News events over the weekend included: earthquakes in two major oil exporting countries -- Iran and Colombia; threats by the new British government to slap sanctions on Nigeria; a blockade by Scottish fishermen at the key North Sea Brent blend loading terminal at Sullom Voe; saber-rattling by a senior U.S. military officer as Iran began war games in the Middle East Gulf; reports of Baghdad build up troops near Kurdish-controlled areas in northern Iraq.
But none of the events posed an immediate threat to supply and there has been no change in the bearish outlook for crude supply which prevailed last week, analysts noted.

Rather, the move was more readily explained as an overdue bounce after crude held twice in early April at $18.96 to form "a perfect bottom," according to Hans Kashyap, a technical analyst at Analytics Research Corp.
A number of stop-loss 'buy' orders were triggered on a break through the $20.50/55 level and new 'longs' came into the market there also, traders said.

Crude fell some way short of the $21.80 target some technical analysts had been looking for Monday and the three-day "relative strength index" (RSI) -- an indicator of 'oversold' or 'overbought' -- was showing nearly 95, above the 90 level which is considered the threshold for overbought.

Tuesday, the American Petroleum Instutite weekly status report, including imports, production levels and inventory movement, is due out. Dealers said they'll be looking particularly at gasoline after recent reports showed a high level of "implied demand" while the Department of Energy has been showing fairly anemic demand.
